This phase is deliberately represented only here (a dated facility_roles/placement row) and not as a lifecycle `intervals` row: it was a small-scale R&D prototype, not a revived full science programme (contrast experiment:supercdms-soudan, which WAS split into its own experiment id because it ran a multi-year science campaign with its own terminal INSPIRE record). Keeping a terminal-status `intervals` row for this phase would conflict with the later, still-active/completed SNOLAB intervals under A3's non-terminal-after-terminal check regardless of `Interval.kind`, since the current validator does not filter that check by kind.
Closed 2025 per the newly fetched 2025 SNOLAB workshop report describing the original DAMIC detector as repurposed into a test stand.

name: DAMIC
notes: Two INSPIRE experiment records exist: the original Fermilab prototype (recid 1108203, FNAL-T-0987, approved 2008-12-15, completed 2012-04-09) and the current SNOLAB programme (recid 1401315). Unlike SuperCDMS-Soudan/SNOLAB (see experiment:supercdms-soudan), the Fermilab prototype is not represented as its own experiment id or as a lifecycle `intervals` row: it was a small-scale R&D device establishing feasibility, not an independent science campaign, so it is recorded only via the dated `facility_roles` row above. `external.inspire_experiment` cites the current (SNOLAB) recid.

RESOLVED by independent verification (2026-09-17 pass): the original research pass recorded status `active` because no source it had fetched stated an end date. A 2025 SNOLAB Future Projects Workshop report (arXiv:2507.11368), fetched during verification, states the original DAMIC detector at SNOLAB has become a test stand for background studies -- i.e. its dark-matter science run is over. Status is now recorded as `completed` with a sourced terminal interval.

2026-09-18 fix: the Fermilab prototype's lifecycle `intervals` row was removed (previously labelled non-terminal `active` through 2012-04 specifically to avoid an A3 non-terminal-after-terminal conflict with the later SNOLAB intervals, despite INSPIRE giving an explicit date_completed for that phase). The underlying fact (2008-12 to 2012-04, at Fermilab) is unchanged and remains fully sourced via `facility_roles`; only its representation moved, per the coordinator's instruction that a prototype phase belongs in a dated placement/facility_role row rather than a mislabelled lifecycle interval.

physics_goals.quote: our data exclude spin-independent WIMP-nucleon scattering cross sections as low as 3x10^-41 cm^2 for WIMPs with masses from 7 to 10 GeV/c^2
value: Search for WIMP and light dark matter via ionization signals in silicon CCDs

summary.plain: DAMIC searched for dark matter using the same kind of light-sensing chips found in digital cameras, cooled and shielded deep underground at SNOLAB in Canada. It started at Fermilab and moved to SNOLAB, later gaining even more sensitive 'skipper' chips, before the detector was repurposed as a background test stand around 2025.
summary.technical: Silicon CCD dark matter search; began as a shallow Fermilab prototype (2008-2012), then operated a tower of seven 16-Mpixel CCDs (~42 g, 11 kg-day exposure) at SNOLAB in 2017-2018, and later two 24-Mpixel skipper CCDs investigating a low-energy ionization excess through at least January 2024. Superseded in name by DAMIC-M at Modane; per a 2025 SNOLAB workshop report, the original SNOLAB detector has since become a test stand for background studies.

unique_capabilities.quote: two silicon charge-coupled devices (CCDs), each with 24 megapixels and skipper readout, deployed in the DAMIC setup at SNOLAB
value: Thick, fully-depleted scientific CCDs with very low dark current, later upgraded to skipper-readout CCDs for single-electron sensitivity
